summary: Alpha glycerylphosphorylcholine (choline alfoscerate, GPC) is a semi-synthetic cholinergic precursor used as an adjunct in cognitive disorders of vascular or degenerative origin. It supplies choline for acetylcholine synthesis and membrane phospholipids. It is not FDA-approved; data derive from EMA/national formularies and clinical studies.
indications: Cognitive impairment associated with cerebrovascular disorders (e.g., post-stroke, multi-infarct)
Mild to moderate degenerative dementia including Alzheimer-type (adjunctive, where marketed)
Memory and behavioral disturbances of the elderly
Pseudodepression and confusional states secondary to cerebrovascular insufficiency

dosage.d: 1000 mg once daily IM or slow IV
dosage.n: Typically 28 days, then switch to oral

admin: Oral capsules/solution usually taken before meals
Parenteral form given by intramuscular injection or slow intravenous infusion
Do not mix parenteral solution with incompatible diluents
Reassess cognitive benefit after a defined treatment course
moa: Provides choline that crosses the blood-brain barrier and is incorporated into membrane phospholipids and into acetylcholine, increasing central cholinergic neurotransmission. The glycerophosphate moiety serves as a precursor for membrane phospholipid synthesis, supporting neuronal membrane integrity.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to choline alfoscerate or excipients

preg: Safety in pregnancy has not been established; use is not recommended unless clearly necessary.
lact: It is not known whether choline alfoscerate passes into breast milk; use during breastfeeding is not recommended.
renal: No specific dose adjustment has been established; use with caution in significant renal impairment.
hepatic: No specific dose adjustment has been established; use with caution in significant hepatic impairment.

moderate: Other cholinergic / cholinesterase-inhibiting agents - additive cholinergic effects
minor: Anticholinergic drugs - may blunt therapeutic effect
interactions.food: No clinically significant food interactions reported.
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction documented; excessive alcohol may worsen cognition.

emergency: Severe allergic reaction (rash, swelling, breathing difficulty)

monitoring: Cognitive and functional status over the treatment course
Signs of cholinergic excess in susceptible patients
counsel: Take as prescribed, typically before meals for oral forms
Report persistent nausea, heartburn or rash
Improvement may be gradual over weeks to months
Inform your doctor of all other medicines, especially other brain/cholinergic drugs
pk: Store at room temperature, protected from light and moisture
pearls: NOTE: Not FDA-approved; information based on EMA/national SmPC, BNF-style sources and clinical trials, not a US FDA label
Also known as choline alfoscerate or GPC
Marketed in several countries as adjunct for cognitive decline; evidence base is limited
Crosses the blood-brain barrier more readily than some other choline sources
missed: Take the missed oral dose when remembered; if it is almost time for the next dose, skip it and resume the usual schedule. Do not double the dose.
overdose: No specific antidote. Overdose may cause cholinergic effects such as nausea, vomiting, salivation, sweating or bradycardia; manage supportively and symptomatically.
